title: Soldi e ambiente
sub: Periodi ipotetici, unless e in case - cosa succede se...
grammar: Zero, first e second conditional, unless, in case, as long as
situation: In banca: aprire un conto e problemi con la carta

lessons.title: Se succede, se succedesse
lessons.intro: In italiano il periodo ipotetico è un incubo di congiuntivi. In inglese è molto più regolare, ma gli italiani sbagliano il tempo dopo if. Qui impari le tre strutture e due parole utili: unless e in case.

steps.title: Zero e first conditional: cose vere e cose probabili
steps.body:
**Zero conditional**: **if + present simple, present simple**. Per fatti sempre veri e regole.
- If you heat ice, it **melts**.
- If I **don't sleep**, I **get** a headache.

**First conditional**: **if + present simple, will + base**. Per una **situazione possibile** nel futuro e la sua conseguenza.
- If it **rains** tomorrow, we'**ll stay** at home.
- If you **save** £50 a month, you'**ll have** £600 in a year.

Nella frase con if **non si mette mai will**: «If I will see him» è l'errore più comune. Nella principale, al posto di will, si possono usare **can, may, might** o un imperativo: *If you see Anna, tell her to call me.*
table: If you mix blue and yellow, you get green.
If I get the job, I'll buy a car.
ex: If you don't pay by the 10th, the bank charges a fee.
Se non paghi entro il 10, la banca applica una commissione.
If I find a bargain, I'll send you the link.
Se trovo un affare, ti mando il link.

steps.title: Second conditional: situazioni immaginarie
steps.body:
**If + past simple, would + base**. Si usa per situazioni **irreali o improbabili nel presente o nel futuro**, che in italiano esprimi con il congiuntivo imperfetto e il condizionale.
- If I **had** more money, I'**d buy** a bigger flat. (ma non ce l'ho)
- If I **won** the lottery, I **would invest** in solar panels.

Con **be** si usa **were** per tutte le persone (anche was è accettato nel parlato): If I **were** you, I'd talk to the manager.

**Errori tipici degli italiani**:
- «If I **would have** more money...» (would nella if clause è sbagliato)
- «If I **will** win...» (will non si usa dopo if)
- usare il present simple nell'if e would nella principale («If I win, I would...»).
table: If I earned more, I would save more.
ex: If I were rich, I wouldn't work so hard.
Se fossi ricco, non lavorerei così tanto.
What would you do if you lost your card?
Che cosa faresti se perdessi la carta?

steps.title: Unless, in case, as long as
steps.body:
- **Unless = if ... not**: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train. (= If you don't hurry...) Dopo unless **non si mette un altro not**: «Unless you don't hurry» è sbagliato.
- **In case + present simple**: per **precauzione**, qualcosa che farai prima, nel caso succeda. I'll take an umbrella **in case it rains**. (lo prendo prima, non dopo che piove). Non va confuso con **if**: I'll take it **if it rains** = lo prendo solo se piove.
- **As long as / provided (that)** = **a condizione che**: You can borrow my car **as long as you drive carefully**.

Dopo tutte queste congiunzioni, come dopo if, si usa il **present simple** per il futuro.
ex: You won't get a refund unless you have the receipt.
Non avrai il rimborso a meno che tu abbia lo scontrino.
Take some cash in case the card machine isn't working.
Porta un po' di contanti nel caso il POS non funzioni.
I'll lend you the money as long as you pay me back soon.
Ti presto i soldi purché me li restituisca presto.

steps.title: Quale tipo scegliere?
steps.body:
Chiediti: la situazione è **sempre vera**, **possibile** o **immaginaria**?
- Sempre vera -> **zero**: If you boil water, it evaporates.
- Possibile / realistica -> **first**: If I get a pay rise, I'll save more.
- Immaginaria / improbabile -> **second**: If I got a pay rise, I would travel more.

La differenza è nell'attitudine di chi parla: «If I win the lottery, I'll buy a house» suona come se ci credessi; «If I won the lottery, I would buy a house» come un sogno.
ex: If I get the money, I'll invest it.
Se ottengo i soldi, li investirò.
If I got the money, I would invest it.
Se ricevessi quei soldi, li investirei.

lessons.title: Soldi e ambiente
lessons.intro: Il lessico per parlare di bilancio personale, di banca e di ambiente: quanto spendi, quanto risparmi e che cosa lasci sul pianeta.

ex: I can't afford a new car on my salary.
Non posso permettermi un'auto nuova con il mio stipendio.
words.note: Si usa quasi sempre con can / can't: can't afford + nome o to + verbo.

ex: We have a tight budget this month.
Questo mese abbiamo un budget molto stretto.
words.note: Anche verbo: budget for = mettere in preventivo. Collocazione: stick to a budget.

ex: Her income is lower than her expenses.
Le sue entrate sono inferiori alle spese.
words.note: Salary = stipendio fisso; income = tutte le entrate.

ex: I withdrew two hundred pounds from the cash machine.
Ho prelevato duecento sterline al bancomat.
words.note: Irregolare: withdraw - withdrew - withdrawn. Il nome è withdrawal.

ex: I'm in my overdraft until the end of the month.
Sono scoperto fino a fine mese.
words.note: Si dice be in your overdraft o go into your overdraft.

ex: There's a small fee for withdrawals abroad.
C'è una piccola commissione per i prelievi all'estero.
words.note: Per i servizi (banca, scuola, medico). Il biglietto è fare.

ex: She invested her savings in solar panels.
Ha investito i risparmi in pannelli solari.
Don't waste water while you brush your teeth.
Non sprecare l'acqua mentre ti lavi i denti.
words.note: Anche nome non numerabile: a waste of time / food waste.

ex: We recycle all our glass and paper.
Ricicliamo tutto il vetro e la carta.
Wind is a renewable energy source.
Il vento è una fonte di energia rinnovabile.
Air pollution is a big problem in the city.
L'inquinamento atmosferico è un grosso problema in città.
Flying less will reduce your carbon footprint.
Volare meno ridurrà la tua impronta di carbonio.
I bought a second-hand bike for fifty pounds.
Ho comprato una bici usata per cinquanta sterline.
words.note: Si usa anche come avverbio: I bought it second-hand.

ex: At ten pounds, this jacket is a real bargain.
A dieci sterline, questa giacca è un vero affare.
words.note: Indica l'acquisto conveniente. Contrattare sul prezzo si dice haggle.

pairs: ridurre la propria impronta di carbonio

steps.s: I can't ___ a new car on my salary.
steps.why: «Permettersi» economicamente = afford. Pay e spend vogliono un'altra costruzione.

steps.s: I bought this jacket for only ten pounds. It was a real ___ .
steps.why: Un acquisto molto conveniente è a bargain. Discount è lo sconto, non l'affare.

steps.s: Some banks ___ a small fee for every withdrawal abroad.
steps.why: Si dice charge a fee: applicare una commissione.

steps.s: Using public transport helps to reduce air ___ in big cities.
steps.why: Serve un nome non numerabile: pollute -> pollution.

steps.s: We need more ___ energy, like sun and wind.
steps.why: Serve un aggettivo: renew -> renewable.

steps.q: Che cosa significa «second-hand» riferito a un'auto?
steps.why: Second-hand = già usato da qualcun altro.

lessons.title: Il vero prezzo della moda economica
lessons.intro: Un articolo di opinione su come risparmiare e inquinare meno cambiando il modo di fare shopping. Cerca i periodi ipotetici e le regole che l'autore si è dato.

steps.title: The hidden price of cheap clothes
steps.text:
A few months ago I counted the clothes in my wardrobe. There were sixty-three items, and I had worn only about twenty of them in the last year. I felt a little embarrassed, because most of those clothes had been cheap bargains: a five-pound T-shirt here, a ten-pound jumper there. If something costs so little, you don't think twice about buying it.

But cheap clothes have a hidden price. The fashion industry produces about a tenth of the world's carbon emissions, and a lot of what we buy ends up in the bin after only a few wears. According to some studies, a single cotton T-shirt needs about two thousand litres of water. If we all bought half as many clothes, the pollution from the industry would fall dramatically.

So what can we do? Some people say that we should simply stop shopping, but that isn't realistic for most of us. Instead, I decided to try a different approach. First, I set a monthly budget: forty pounds, and not a penny more. Second, I made a rule that I would only buy something if I could imagine wearing it at least thirty times. Finally, I started looking in second-hand shops and online markets. I was surprised by how many good things you can find there. Last week I bought a wool coat for eighteen pounds that would cost over a hundred in a normal shop.

My friend Laura thinks I'm being too strict. "You'll get bored," she says, "unless you allow yourself a treat now and then." She may be right, so I have agreed to buy one new item every season. In case I forget the rules, I've written them on a note inside the wardrobe door.

I'm not trying to be perfect. But I now believe that if we spent more on fewer, better things, we would save money and help the planet at the same time.

The clothes had been very expensive.
qs.why: «I had worn only about twenty of them in the last year».

qs.why: «The pollution from the industry would fall dramatically».

qs.why: «forty pounds, and not a penny more».

qs.q: What is the writer's rule for buying clothes?

Never buy more than one item a month.
Only buy things under ten pounds.
qs.why: «I would only buy something if I could imagine wearing it at least thirty times».

opts: The writer will get bored without a treat.
The writer should stop shopping completely.
Second-hand clothes are a bad idea.
qs.why: «You'll get bored unless you allow yourself a treat now and then».

qs.q: The writer has now stopped buying new clothes completely.
qs.why: Ha accettato di comprare un capo nuovo a ogni stagione.

steps.s: Last week I bought a coat that ___ over a hundred pounds in a normal shop.
steps.why: Il prezzo ipotetico in un negozio normale: would + base.

steps.why: Wardrobe = armadio.

lessons.title: Meno spese, meno plastica
lessons.intro: Due amici parlano di come tengono sotto controllo le spese e di come riciclano. Ascolta i piccoli trucchi quotidiani e le condizioni che pongono.

steps.title: Saving money and plastic
steps.it: Ascolta il dialogo e rispondi. Puoi riascoltarlo e usare la velocità lenta.
lines: Jack, have you seen my bank statement? I don't understand where all my money goes.
Well, if you spend like me, it just disappears. I've started using an app that tracks every payment. It shows you everything.
Honestly, yes. Last month I realised I was spending sixty pounds on takeaway coffee. If I stopped buying them, I'd save over seven hundred a year.
Exactly. So now I make coffee at home and I take it in a flask. Unless it's an emergency, I don't buy any.
I should do the same. What about the environment? You told me you're trying to recycle more.
Yes, but it's harder than it sounds. In my building there's only one bin, so I take my plastic bottles to the supermarket. I always take a bag with me, in case I find some more on the way.
If you put the bag next to your front door, you won't forget. That's my trick.
Okay, I'll try. And if it doesn't work, I'll blame you!

opts: She doesn't know where her money goes.
She has lost her bank card.
She spends too much on coffee.

How much could Jack save in a year?
Why does Jack take plastic bottles to the supermarket?

lessons.title: In banca
lessons.intro: Aprire un conto, chiedere delle commissioni, bloccare una carta inghiottita dal bancomat. Le frasi per cavartela in banca in inglese senza tradurre dall'italiano.

steps.title: Aprire un conto
steps.body:
- **I'd like to open a current account.** = Vorrei aprire un conto corrente. (current account; savings account = conto di risparmio)
- **What do I need to bring?** / **Do you need proof of address?**
- **Is there a monthly fee?** = C'è un canone mensile?
- **Can I get a debit card with it?**
- **How long will it take to open?**

Attenzione: «conto» è **account**, mentre **bill** è la fattura o la bolletta (a gas bill). «Carta di credito» è credit card, ma la carta del conto corrente è la **debit card**.
ex: I'd like to open a current account, please.
Vorrei aprire un conto corrente, per favore.
Is there a monthly fee?
C'è un canone mensile?

steps.title: Problemi con la carta
steps.body:
- **My card has been swallowed by the cash machine.** (ATM = cash machine / cashpoint)
- **I've lost my card. Could you block it, please?**
- **My card was declined.** = Il pagamento è stato rifiutato.
- **There's a payment I don't recognise on my statement.**
- **Could you send me a replacement card?**

Tono: **Could you...? / Would it be possible to...?** sono cortesi; «You must...» è troppo diretto e non aiuta. Per ringraziare: **That would be very helpful, thank you.**
ex: My card was declined at the supermarket.
La mia carta è stata rifiutata al supermercato.
Could you block it and send me a replacement?
Potrebbe bloccarla e mandarmene una nuova?

steps.title: Aprire un conto
steps.it: Scegli la battuta più naturale e cortese (Tu).

lessons.title: Un articolo di opinione
lessons.intro: Scriverai un breve articolo d'opinione su un tema di attualità, usando i periodi ipotetici per proporre idee e conseguenze. Prima prepari struttura e connettivi.

steps.title: Come si scrive un articolo d'opinione
steps.body:
Struttura in 3-4 paragrafi brevi:
- **Titolo** (una domanda funziona bene)
- **Opinione chiara**: In my opinion, ... / I strongly believe that...
- **Argomento e conseguenza**: If people have to pay, they will think twice.
- **Obiezione e risposta**: Some people say that... However, ...
- **Conclusione**: To sum up, ... / All in all, ...

**Connettivi**: On the one hand... on the other hand, However, Therefore, For example, Unless we..., As long as...

Per dare un consiglio o proporre una soluzione: **If I were the government, I would...**
ex: If shops charged for bags, people would use fewer.
Se i negozi facessero pagare le borse, la gente ne userebbe di meno.
Unless we act now, the problem will get worse.
Se non agiamo ora, il problema peggiorerà.

steps.s: ___ the one hand, plastic bags are cheap; on the other hand, they harm the sea.
steps.why: L'espressione è on the one hand... on the other hand.

steps.s: Some people think that prices will go up. ___ , I believe the benefits are bigger.
steps.why: However introduce un'obiezione o un contrasto con la frase precedente.

steps.s: If I would be the mayor, I would ban cars in the city centre.
answers: If I were the mayor, I would ban cars in the city centre
If I was the mayor, I would ban cars in the city centre
steps.why: Nell'if clause: past simple (were), non would.

steps.s: In my ___ , shops should charge for plastic bags.
steps.why: In my opinion / In my view: per esprimere il proprio parere.

steps.s1: If we don't change our habits, the seas will be full of plastic.
steps.s2: The seas will be full of plastic ___ our habits.
steps.why: Unless = if ... not, e il verbo resta affermativo.

steps.q: A school magazine is asking readers for short articles. Write an article answering the question: Should shops charge for plastic bags? Give your opinion, support it with reasons and say what you would do if you were in charge.
steps.it: Scrivi un breve articolo d'opinione sul tema «Should shops charge for plastic bags?»: dai la tua opinione, motivala e di' che cosa faresti se fossi il responsabile.
checklist: Ho messo un titolo e organizzato il testo in paragrafi
Ho espresso chiaramente la mia opinione (In my opinion...)
Ho usato almeno un first conditional e un second conditional
Ho usato unless o in case almeno una volta
Ho aggiunto un'obiezione con However o some people say...
useful: If people have to pay, they will...
If I were the government, I would...
steps.model:
Should shops charge for plastic bags?

In my opinion, shops should definitely charge for plastic bags. If people have to pay even a few pence, they will think twice and bring their own bags. In my town, bag use fell by half after the new rule.

Some people say that this is unfair to customers on low incomes. However, if you reuse one strong bag, you save money in the long run.

If I were the government, I would go even further and ban single-use plastic completely. Unless we change our habits now, our seas will be full of plastic in the future.

To sum up, small charges can bring big changes.

steps.q: What would you do if you had a lot more money?
steps.it: Che cosa faresti se avessi molti più soldi? Usa il second conditional (almeno 4 frasi).
hints: If I had more money, I would...
steps.model: If I had a lot more money, I would first pay off my debts. Then I would invest in a small flat, because I wouldn't have to pay rent any more. I would also travel more, but I wouldn't fly everywhere because I care about the environment. And if I were really rich, I would give some money to a charity that plants trees.

steps.q: What can ordinary people do to protect the environment?
steps.it: Che cosa possono fare le persone comuni per proteggere l'ambiente? Usa first conditional, unless o in case (almeno 4 frasi).
steps.model: If we all use less plastic, the sea will be cleaner. I always take a cloth bag to the supermarket in case I buy something. Unless we change how we travel, pollution will keep getting worse, so I walk or cycle when I can. And as long as it's possible, I buy second-hand clothes.
